lines.phonemes: bɪfˌɔː hiː lˈɛft, nˈɑːdiə plˈeɪst ðə kɹˈaʊn bˈak ˌɒn məhˈamɪd ʃˈɑːz hˈɛd. hiː lˈɛft hˌɪm ˌɒn ɐ θɹˈəʊn wɪðˌaʊt ɪts tɹˈɛʒə.

lines.text: Nadir Shah went home in May. But he had shown everyone — Afghans, Marathas, even a company of merchants — that Delhi could be taken.
lines.tts: Nadir Shah went home in May. But he had shown everyone, Afghans, Marathas, even a company of merchants, that Delhi could be taken.
lines.phonemes: nˈɑːdiə ʃˈɑː wɛnt hˈəʊm ɪn mˈeɪ. bˌʌt hiː had ʃˈəʊn ˈɛvɹɪwˌɒn, ˈafɡanz, mɐɹˈɑːtəz, ˈiːvən ɐ kˈʌmpəni ɒv mˈɜːtʃənts, ðat dˈɛli kʊd biː tˈeɪkən.

lines.text: The historian Jon Wilson, in his book India Conquered, puts it like this.
lines.tts: The historian Jon Wilson, in his book India Conquered, puts it like this.
lines.phonemes: ðə hɪstˈɔːɹiən dʒˈɒn wˈɪlsən, ɪn hɪz bˈʊk ˈɪndiə kˈɒŋkəd, pˌʊts ɪt lˈaɪk ðˈɪs.

lines.text: “Nader Shah was Mughal emperor for only fifty-seven days, in 1739, but those days created aftershocks that transformed India's politics…
lines.tts: Nader Shah was Mughal emperor for only fifty-seven days, in seventeen thirty-nine, but those days created aftershocks that transformed India's politics.
lines.phonemes: nˈɑːdiə ʃˈɑː wɒz mˈuːɡʌl ˈɛmpəɹə fɔːɹ ˈəʊnli fˈɪftisˈɛvən dˈeɪz, ɪn sˈɛvəntˌiːn θˈɜːtinˈaɪn, bˌʌt ðəʊz dˈeɪz kɹiːˈeɪtɪd ˈaftəʃˌɒks ðat tɹansfˈɔːmd ˈɪndiəz pˈɒlətˌɪks.

lines.text: Those fifty-seven days laid the ground which allowed the East India Company to conquer territory in India for the first time.”
lines.tts: Those fifty-seven days laid the ground which allowed the East India Company to conquer territory in India for the first time.
lines.phonemes: ðəʊz fˈɪftisˈɛvən dˈeɪz lˈeɪd ðə ɡɹˈaʊnd wˌɪtʃ ɐlˈaʊd ðɪ ˈiːst ˈɪndiə kˈʌmpəni tə kˈɒŋkə tˈɛɹɪtəɹi ɪn ˈɪndiə fəðə fˈɜːst tˈaɪm.

lines.text: How could a Persian raid help a British trading company?
lines.tts: How could a Persian raid help a British trading company?
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ kʊd ɐ pˈɜːʒən ɹˈeɪd hˈɛlp ɐ bɹˈɪtɪʃ tɹˈeɪdɪŋ kˈʌmpəni?

lines.text: Because the money was gone. Delhi could no longer pay its armies or reward the governors who stayed loyal.
lines.tts: Because the money was gone. Delhi could no longer pay its armies or reward the governors who stayed loyal.
lines.phonemes: bɪkˈɒz ðə mˈʌni wɒz ɡˈɒn. dˈɛli kʊd nˌəʊ lˈɒŋɡə pˈeɪ ɪts ˈɑːmiz ɔː ɹɪwˈɔːd ðə ɡˈʌvənəz hˌuː stˈeɪd lˈɔɪəl.

lines.text: So the governors stopped waiting for orders. Hyderabad, Bengal and Awadh ran their own affairs, and the Marathas pushed further north.
lines.tts: So the governors stopped waiting for orders. Hyderabad, Bengal and Awadh ran their own affairs, and the Marathas pushed further north.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ ðə ɡˈʌvənəz stˈɒpt wˈeɪtɪŋ fɔːɹ ˈɔːdəz. hˈaɪdəɹɐbˌad, bˌɛŋɡˈɔːl and ɐwˈʌd ɹˈan ðeəɹ ˈəʊn ɐfˈeəz, and ðə mɐɹˈɑːtəz pˈʊʃt fˈɜːðə nˈɔːθ.

lines.text: In a land of rival rulers, a company with ships, guns and hired soldiers could pick a side, and in time take land for itself.
lines.tts: In a land of rival rulers, a company with ships, guns and hired soldiers could pick a side, and in time take land for itself.
lines.phonemes: ɪn ɐ lˈand ɒv ɹˈaɪvəl ɹˈuːləz, ɐ kˈʌmpəni wɪð ʃˈɪps, ɡˈʌnz and hˈaɪəd sˈəʊldʒəz kʊd pˈɪk ɐ sˈaɪd, and ɪn tˈaɪm tˈeɪk lˈand fɔːɹ ɪtsˈɛlf.

lines.text: Not every historian gives fifty-seven days that much weight. Many point to a decline that began long before Nadir Shah.
lines.tts: Not every historian gives fifty-seven days that much weight. Many point to a decline that began long before Nadir Shah.
lines.phonemes: nˌɒt ˈɛvɹɪ hɪstˈɔːɹiən ɡˈɪvz fˈɪftisˈɛvən dˈeɪz ðat mˈʌtʃ wˈeɪt. mˈɛni pˈɔɪnt tʊ ɐ dɪklˈaɪn ðat bɪɡˈan lˈɒŋ bɪfˈɔː nˈɑːdiə ʃˈɑː.

lines.text: But here is what 1739 really shows.
lines.tts: But here is what seventeen thirty-nine really shows.
lines.phonemes: bˌʌt hˈiəɹ ɪz wɒt sˈɛvəntˌiːn θˈɜːtinˈaɪn ɹˈiəlɪ ʃˈəʊz.

lines.text: An empire's greatest treasure is not its gold. It is the belief that it cannot be touched.
lines.tts: An empire's greatest treasure is not its gold. It is the belief that it cannot be touched.
lines.phonemes: ɐn ˈɛmpaɪəz ɡɹˈeɪtɪst tɹˈɛʒəɹ ɪz nˌɒt ɪts ɡˈəʊld. ɪt ɪz ðə bɪlˈiːf ðˌatɪt kˈanɒt biː tˈʌtʃt.

lines.text: Nadir Shah carried off a throne and a diamond. What he really took was that belief. And once it was gone, every rival moved at once.
lines.tts: Nadir Shah carried off a throne and a diamond. What he really took was that belief. And once it was gone, every rival moved at once.
lines.phonemes: nˈɑːdiə ʃˈɑː kˈaɹid ˈɒf ɐ θɹˈəʊn and ɐ dˈaɪəmənd. wˌɒt hiː ɹˈiəlɪ tˈʊk wɒz ðat bɪlˈiːf. and wˈʌns ɪt wɒz ɡˈɒn, ˈɛvɹɪ ɹˈaɪvəl mˈuːvd ɐtwˈɒns.

lines.text: So, was Nadir Shah's invasion the real beginning of British India? Tell me what you think in the comments.
lines.tts: So, was Nadir Shah's invasion the real beginning of British India? Tell me what you think in the comments.
lines.phonemes: sˈəʊ, wɒz nˈɑːdiə ʃˈɑːz ɪnvˈeɪʒən ðə ɹˈiəl bɪɡˈɪnɪŋ ɒv bɹˈɪtɪʃ ˈɪndiə? tˈɛl mˌiː wɒt juː θˈɪŋk ɪnðə kˈɒmɛnts.

lines.text: Eight years later, Nadir Shah was dead. One of his commanders, an Afghan named Ahmad Shah Abdali, would come back again and again — until a battlefield called Panipat.
lines.tts: Eight years later, Nadir Shah was dead. One of his commanders, an Afghan named Ahmad Shah Abdali, would come back again and again, until a battlefield called Panipat.
